RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the October 20, 2008/Asvina 28, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development; Law
and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable Energy; Power;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and Child
Development)
Total number of questions — 20
8
Development of Chiria Mines
*21. SHRI JAI PRAKASH
NARAYAN SINGH:
SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that M/s. Arcelor
Mittal has shown interest in joining hands
with Steel Authority of India Ltd. (SAIL),
and is open for a Joint Venture (JV)
agreement for developing the Chiria Mines;
(b) if so, the complete details in this
regard; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
resolve the ongoing dispute between SAIL
and the Jharkhand Government over Chiria
Mines?
Beggars selling children in Kolkata
†*22. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that beggars are
selling children in Kolkata;
(b) whether it is also a fact that this
practice is not being controlled due to
corruption; and
(c) if so, the details in this regard?
Judges (Inquiry) Bill
*23. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Bill, empowering the
people to complain against corrupt Judges,
would remain a pipe-dream as Government
is reportedly succumbing to pressure from
some of its allies, keen to avoid a
confrontation with the judiciary;
(b) whether this move is bound to raise
eye-brows because the Supreme Court is at
present struggling to constitute a probe panel
into the multicrore Ghaziabad Provident
Funds Scam, in which 36 Judges of the Apex
Court are allegedly involved; and
(c) if so, whether Government proposes
to shelve the Judges (Inquiry) Bill from
becoming a law and if so, the reasons
therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

9
Collaboration with foreign
technological universities
*24. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR:
SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to allow
foreign technological universities to
collaborate with Indian universities and
institutes, to conduct joint programmes;
(b) whether suitable regulations in this
regard have been brought out by
Government; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Overdrawal of electricity from the grid
*25. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (CERC) has issued
directions to State Governments to curb
overdrawal of power/electricity from the
Grid;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether inspite of directions by the
CERC, the States are violating the Indian
Electricity Grid Code and are ignoring the
instructions of the Regional Load Despatch
Centres (RLDC); and
(d) if so, the concrete steps Government
proposes to take in this regard?
Chinese power plants in India
*26. SHRI HARISH RAWA T:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Central Electricity
Authority has set up a Committee to probe
the technical quality of the Chinese plants
installed in India;
(b) if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c) whether permission to the Chinese
firms to set up power plants in the country
is posing threat to the security of the
country; and
(d) if so, the facts thereof and the steps
taken by Government to ensure that such
permission to the Chinese firms does not
pose any threat to the country?
Infrastructural facilities and human
resources in higher education
†*27. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the amount required for establishing
infrastructural facilities and human
resources for teaching to achieve the higher
education,  target of 15 per cent separately,
and in which manner and from which
sources the same would be raised;
(b) the projection as to the number of
students likely to opt for technical
education in the field of higher education
and the number of industrial establishments
which have agreed to co-opt in this field;
and
(c) whether it is a fact that the policy of
reservation for SCs/STs in technical
institutions has been a failure and their
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

10
dropout rate is increasing; if so, the plan of
Government in this regard?

CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Government of India has entered into a new
agreement with UNICEF to check violence
against children and reduce the rate of HIV/
AIDS among adol
